title.narrative: Svenska Röda Korset: Påverkansarbete för Migranters rättigheter
Swedish Red Cross: Advocating for Migrants' Rights

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the project "Advocating for migrants' rights and dignity", implemented by the Swedish Red Cross and the Red Cross Migration Network in Latin America, is that the rights of women, children and men who migrate are bolstered in line with international humanitarian and human rights legislation.
This overall objective is underpinned by two specific outcomes:
Outcome 1: A stronger regional migration network with increased coordination and capacity to advocate for migrants rights.
Outcome 2: Improved inclusion of migrants voices, needs and rights in national and regional decision making.

Detta projekt gäller stöd till Svenska Röda Korset för projektet Advocating for migrants’ rights and dignity under treårsperioden 2024-2026. Den totala budgeten är 10 MSEK och Sida är enda givare till projektet. Det övergripande målet är att stärka rättigheter, i linje med internationell humanitär rätt och konventioner om mänskliga rättigheter, för kvinnor, barn och män som migrerar Projektets förväntade resultat är: - Ett starkare regionalt migrationsnätverk inom Röda Korsrörelsen med ökad samordning och kapacitet att verka för migranters rättigheter. - Att migranters röster, behov och rättigheter inkluderas i nationellt och regionalt beslutsfattande som rör dem. Svenska Röda Korset genomför projektet i samarbete med det regionala migrationsnätverk som består av tolv nationella Röda Korsföreningar i Latinamerika. Colombianska Röda Korset har rollen som sekretariat för nätverket. Projektet syftar till att driva och stärka påverkansarbete och humanitär diplomati inom Röda Korsets regionala nätverk för migration och därigenom säkerställa att kvinnor, barn och män som migrerar kan åtnjuta sina rättigheter i enlighet med humanitär rätt och MR-lagstiftning. För att uppnå detta kommer nätverket tillvarata erfarenheter och främja möjligheter till deltagande för kvinnor, barn och män som migrerar. Projektet kommer att samverka med lokala migrantorganisationer för att gemensamt identifiera de behov och rättigheter som drivs gentemot beslutsfattare och för gemensamt deltagande i påverkansarbete. Medlemmarna i nätverket kommer, tillsammans med migrantorganisationer och andra humanitära aktörer, att försöka påverka nationella lagar och regionala policyer till stöd för migranters rättigheter tillgång till viktiga samhällstjänster. Ett evidensbaserat narrativ kommer att utvecklas för att möjliggöra och stärka ett koordinerat påverkansarbete gentemot regeringar för att påverka lagar, policyer och praxis av vikt för migranters rättigheter. Genom detta förväntas uppnås en bättre förståelse hos beslutsfattare för migranters behov och utmaningar under hela migrationsprocessen. Myndigheter kommer att erinras om det ansvar som åligger dem för att bidra till att migranter kan åtnjuta sina rättigheter och ges skydd. Förutom dessa prioriteringar kommer nätverket att förespråka hållbara lösningar, såsom lokal integration, migranters tillgång till grundläggande samhällstjänster, sysselsättning, familjeåterförening och säker rättslig status, såväl utifrån lokala kontexter som med ett regionalt perspektiv. Lösningar och positiva narrativ kring migration kommer att utformas och drivas för att bidra till ökad inkludering som främjar migranters möjligheter att bidra till samhällsutveckling. Det regionala migrationsnätverket kommer att få stöd och stärkas genom tillgång till såväl verktyg som kapacitetsutveckling för arbetet med humanitär diplomati. Projektet förväntas har störst inflytande i norra Sydamerika och Centralamerika, samtidigt som det regionala perspektivet är av vikt.

This project Advocating for migrants’ rights and dignity is implemented by the Swedish Red Cross during 2024- 2026 with a budget of 10 MSEK. The overall objective is that the rights of women, children and men who migrate are bolstered in line with international humanitarian and human rights legislation. This overall objective is underpinned by two specific outcomes: - A stronger regional migration network with increased coordination and capacity to advocate for migrants’ rights. - Improved inclusion of migrants’ voices, needs and rights in national and regional decision-making. The Swedish Red Cross implement the project together with the regional migration network composed by twelve Red Cross National Societies in Latin America. The Colombian Red Cross host the secretariat for the network. The project will advance and strengthen the advocacy and humanitarian diplomacy efforts of the Red Cross regional network for migration to ensure that migrants can enjoy their rights in accordance with humanitarian and human rights law. The migrants themselves are an integral part of the project and the project will seek to capture their experiences and pressing needs in each territory. The project will also involve local migrant organizations to identify needs and rights to be advocated for towards decision-makers, as well as for participation in advocacy roundtable-discussions. Together with migrant organizations and other humanitarian actors, the members of the network will advocate towards decision-makers and seek to influence national laws and regional policies to support migrants’ rights as well as their safe and effective access to essential services. An evidence-based narrative will be developed to enable meaningful, coordinated engagement with governments and influence migration-related laws, policies and practice. The aim is to enable a better understanding by decision-makers of migrants’ needs and challenges throughout migratory routes, recalling authorities of their responsibilities, including measures to protect migrants. These are key priorities as well as advocating for sustainable solutions, such as local integration, access to basic services, employment, family reunification and secure legal status, based on local experiences and promoting a regional perspective. Solutions and positive narratives around migration will be promoted to enhance the inclusion of, and enable women, children and men who migrate the opportunities to contribute to the development of society. The network will be supported and strengthened through tools-, skills- and capacity development in humanitarian diplomacy. While pursuing a regional approach, the project will have the greatest influence in Northern South America and Central America.

Decision on Contribution - Swedish Red Cross

description.narrative:
In this second year of the project, the partner reports three main achievements.
Firstly, the Red Cross Regional Migration Network for the Americas and Caribbean, REDMAC, was formally established in April 2025. REDMAC currently consists of 20 National Societies in the region, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), he International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), and is supported by several Partner National Societies (PNS). With the formal establishment of REDMAC, its members have further strengthened and coordinated actions in the field of migration, through a cross-border, regional approach. It has also provided space for sharing context analyses and strengthening technical and operational capacities to provide a comprehensive and relevant response.
A second achievement has been the work on humanitarian diplomacy both internally and externally. With the aim of raising, listening and responding to the voices of migrants, the network has continued to meet with various migrant organisations in the Americas and the Caribbean. The meetings made it possible to identify needs, barriers to accessing rights, and protection risks of different migrant profiles throughout the region. The information was then used to create evidence-based advocacy messages that were shared in various forums and meetings with stakeholders and decision-makers. Several meetings were held with regional and international organizations such as Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (CELAC), the Global Forum on Migration and Development and the Cartagena 40.
The third key achievement for 2025 was the generation of collective learning products such as the design and development of the e-learning course Humanitarian Diplomacy with an Emphasis on Migration. It aims to strengthen REDMAC's capacities in humanitarian diplomacy in relation to migration. The e-learning course was developed during 2025 and is expected to be launched in the first quarter of 2026. Its main audience are volunteers and staff of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. Furthermore, the dashboard or data collection tool set up in 2024, which provides data and context analysis per country, is regularly being used and updated to visualise data and context analysis by country. It enables REDMAC members to make evidence-based decisions and plan humanitarian diplomacy actions.
REDMACs work in 2025 contributed to several tangible changes in policy, access, and protection for migrants across the region. The most direct impact was seen in Colombia, where coordinated humanitarian diplomacy and evidence gathered through migrant-led organizations supported the adjustment of Law 1565, removing the three year requirement for returnees to access benefits - an important step toward improving regularization pathways and access to rights. In Mexico, an event in Nogales enabled migrants to present evidence directly to authorities and the U.S. Consulate, resulting in the removal of specific administrative barriers that had restricted access to services for people waiting at the border. At the regional level, REDMACs evidence-based messages - rooted in testimonies and participatory mapping - were incorporated into high level processes such as Cartagena 40, influencing the Chile Declaration and its commitments on protection, health, education, and regularization. These achievements demonstrate that REDMACs strengthened coordination and humanitarian diplomacy capacities are not only elevating migrant voices but also shaping concrete policy outcomes and improving access to rights across multiple countries.
